project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 326 (System persists an automatic demotion when live information coefficient falls below 40 percent of its backtest value)
project_specification.addition_summary:
Implement app_spec.xml feature 326 in the existing risk member (packages/risk, import name risk; seat src/app/modules/risk), which depends on feature 323: *System persists an automatic demotion when live information coefficient falls below 40 percent of its backtest value.*
The feature is the risk supervisor's fourth trigger — the row of docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §13.3's trigger table whose action is *"Auto-demote the signal"*, sitting beside the equity floor, the daily loss, the feed staleness and the clock skew the member already owns. It is the second of the two triggers (the clock skew, feature 329, is the first) whose act is not a halt of the order layer but a *demotion of a signal*: the supervisor measures a promoted signal's live information coefficient against the backtest coefficient it was promoted on, and when the live coefficient falls below 40 percent of the backtest one, it persists a demotion of that signal. The 40 percent line and the "demote automatically" consequence are the spec's own two clauses (docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §475: *"if live IC falls below 40% of backtest IC over a statistically meaningful window, demote automatically"*).
The two operands are **read**, never stated by this feature, and both live in the forward member's forward_record table: the live information coefficient is feature 333's column (the mean of the observed rows), and the backtest coefficient is feature 337's column (the figure landed once on the record's opening row). Feature 337 already computes the quotient — live IC divided by backtest IC, per signal — and answers IcRetention carrying the ratio; this feature takes that ratio as its single input and judges it against the 40 percent line. So feature 326 does not recompute the retention, does not re-read the forward member's columns and does not name them: it reaches the ratio through the forward member's own public seam, exactly as a risk member that must not import a sibling's tables must — it asks the forward member's module-level function for the figure and judges the figure it is handed.
**The verb is *persists*, and that is the whole of the act.** A demotion is a durable fact about a signal — the supervisor's decision that the signal no longer holds its promotion — and a demotion that lived only in a process's memory would be undone by the process's restart, which is the failure the demotion exists to survive. So the demotion lands in a table of this feature's own, one row per demotion, in the workspace's relational store (DATABASE_URL), the same store the member's other persisted acts write. The table is this feature's own, not a column on the forward member's record and not a row in the kill channel's table: the demotion is a *signal* event, not a *record* fact and not an *order layer* state, and forcing it into either of those shapes would break the law the other exists to hold.
**The comparison is strictly `<`, on the ratio the forward member hands over.** The demotion fires when the live IC is *below* 40 percent of the backtest IC — when the retention ratio is strictly less than 0.4 — the workspace's boundary convention beside it (feature 314's strict `<`, feature 312's neighbour rule, feature 329's and feature 328's `>`): a ratio exactly at 40 percent is *at* the line, and the signal is held rather than demoted. The 40 percent is a **constant of this module**, not configuration: the spec names the number ("40 percent") and names no knob to retune it, so it is spelled once as the module's own DEMOTION_BOUND and a supervisor that guessed a bound would demote on a line nobody specified.
**The demotion carries the signal, the ratio, the bound and the moment, and the moment is read back from the demotion's own row.** One row per demotion carries the node_id of the demoted signal, the retention ratio it was demoted under, the bound it fell below, and the instant the demotion was recorded — read back from the standing row rather than stamped here, so the recorded moment and the row are one fact. The demotion is monotone per signal: a signal that has been demoted stays demoted, and a second demotion of the same signal writes nothing and returns the standing demotion with changed=False, the same first-write- wins law feature 322's kill channel holds — a demotion that a later measurement could move would quietly rewrite the record of when the signal lost its promotion.
The member already holds every piece the demotion composes — the relational store addressed by DATABASE_URL, the process-identity label (risk._identity), the error taxonomy (risk.errors) and the store- addressing, ISO-rendering and validation helpers every store in the member restates — so feature 326 adds one module, one table, one value, one store and one module-level spelling, and no new error class beyond what the taxonomy already carries: the address and persistence faults are RiskStoreError, and this feature's own terms (a node that is not a signal identity, a ratio that is not a number, a bound that is not a band, a stored row no demotion can be reconstructed as) are refused in the member's base RiskError where the member's watchdogs that persist nothing already refuse, or in a sibling of RiskStoreError whose noun is the demotion. The forward member's behaviour, messages, codes and tests are untouched: this feature reads the ratio through the forward member's public seam and judges it, and nothing this feature does reaches into the forward member's tables.
project_specification.existing_context:
The risk member (packages/risk, import name risk) is the category "Risk Supervisor & Kill Switches". It already holds the kill channel (feature 322, risk.kill), the halt door (feature 323, risk.halt), the equity floor (feature 324), the manual reset (feature 325), the feed staleness watchdog (feature 328, risk.feed_staleness), the clock skew measurement (feature 329, risk.clock_skew), the flatten (feature 330, risk.flatten) and the halt event ledger (feature 331, risk.halt_events). The member's tables — risk_order_kill, risk_halt_event, risk_clock_skew — are each one module's own, addressed by DATABASE_URL, schema-created idempotently on connect, never a migration. The member's value layer re-derives every stored figure on the way back from a row, so a row edited outside the package fails to reconstruct rather than loading as a plausible-looking fact. The member's module-level spellings open each store from the environment, refusing on the writer's side and answering the empty truth on the reader's side.
The forward member (packages/forward, import name forward) holds the forward_record table and the retention criterion (feature 337, forward.retention). Its module-level function forward_ic_retention (node_id, *, database_url=None, env=None) computes one signal's forward IC retention and answers IcRetention carrying .ratio, .node_id, .live_ic, .backtest_ic, .observed_days and the two instants. It refuses (ForwardRetentionError) when the node has no record, has no observation, has no backtest IC, or has a zero backtest IC. A member never imports another member's tables, so feature 326 reaches the ratio through this public function rather than reading forward_record itself.
The seat (src/app/modules/risk/__init__.py) exposes one accessor per member question, all taking no app argument, resolving from DATABASE_URL. The member's __init__ registers four components (@register) under the names risk, risk-halt-events, risk-flattener and risk-halt — the switch, the ledger, the flattener and the halt door — and the member's suite pins exactly those four build_ builders, so feature 326 adds no fifth. The demotion store is reached through the module-level spellings and RiskSignalDemotionStore.resolve, exactly as clock_skew is; @register lives only in __init__, never a submodule.

category.name: Risk Supervisor & Kill Switches
category.feature:
System persists an automatic demotion when live information coefficient falls below 40 percent of its backtest value.
A new module packages/risk/src/risk/demotion.py (feature 326) holding: the DEMOTION_BOUND constant (0.4); the RISK_SIGNAL_DEMOTION_TABLE table name and its DDL (one row per demotion: a per-signal singleton primary key keyed by node_id, carrying the retention ratio, the bound, the demoted_at moment read back from the row and the recording process identity, with CHECK constraints on the bound and the ratio being a real number); a frozen value SignalDemotion (node_id, ratio, bound, demoted_at, supervisor_process_id, changed) whose __post_init__ re-derives the ratio-against-bound comparison and validates the node identity, the ratio, the bound and the instant; a store RiskSignalDemotionStore (record_demotion judging the ratio against the bound and persisting when below, demotions reading the standing demotion for a signal, demotion_for checking one signal, all over DATABASE_URL, schema-created idempotently, first-write-wins per signal, the demotion moment read back from the standing row); and the module-level spellings demote_on_ic_drop (refuses when no store is named and the ratio is below the bound) and recorded_demotions (answers the empty tuple when no store is named).
The demotion reaches the retention ratio through the forward member's public module-level function forward_ic_retention, never importing the forward member's tables or naming its columns. The store's record method takes the node_id and the ratio (the caller having obtained the ratio from the forward member), judges the ratio against DEMOTION_BOUND with a strict `<`, and persists a row only when below.
The member's __init__ re-exports the new module's public names and the new error class and code, exactly as clock_skew's names are re-exported. The demotion store registers **no component and no builder** — the member's suite pins exactly four build_ builders (the switch, the ledger, the flattener and the halt door), and clock_skew is the precedent this feature follows: it persists a table but is reached through the module-level spellings and RiskSignalDemotionStore.resolve, not through composition. The demotion is the supervisor's own act on its own process over DATABASE_URL, and the process that must survive a restart is the one that must not be required to have composed anything.
A new suite packages/risk/tests/test_demotion.py organised around the sentence's claims — below the bound demotes and persists one row per signal, at or above the bound demotes nothing, the boundary is pinned exactly at 0.4, the demotion carries the ratio and the bound and the moment read back from the row, the moment and the row are one fact, the second demotion of a signal is first-write-wins, the read refuses a row no demotion can be reconstructed as (including past PRAGMA ignore_check_constraints), the store refuses a node that is not a signal identity and a ratio that is not a number, the module-level spelling refuses when no store is named and the ratio is below the bound and answers the empty tuple when no store is named, and the demotion reaches the ratio through the forward member's public seam (a real second interpreter computing the ratio the demotion judges).

project_specification.integration_points: Reads the forward member's public module-level function forward_ic_retention (feature 337) for the retention ratio, never the forward member's tables. Persists in the workspace's relational store (DATABASE_URL) in a table of its own. Uses the member's own process identity (risk._identity.process_identity) and error taxonomy (risk.errors). Registers no component — the member's suite pins exactly four build_ builders, and the demotion is reached through the module-level spelling and RiskSignalDemotionStore.resolve, exactly as clock_skew is. The seat is not extended: the demotion is reached through the member's module-level spelling, not a new seat accessor, because the demotion is the supervisor's own act on its own process, not a per-process resolution the order layer consults.
project_specification.conventions: - Restate DATABASE_URL_ENV, _sqlite_path, _isoformat_utc, _require_aware, _require_real and _require_text in the new module rather than importing them from a sibling, the stance every store in the member takes. - The comparison is strictly `<` (a ratio at the bound is held, not demoted), matching feature 314's strict `<` and the member's boundary convention. - The 40 percent bound is a module constant (DEMOTION_BOUND = 0.4), not configuration. - The demotion moment (demoted_at) is read back from the standing row, never stamped, so the moment and the row are one fact. - First-write-wins per signal: the table's primary key is node_id, so a second demotion of the same signal writes nothing and returns the standing demotion with changed=False. - The value layer re-derives the ratio-against-bound comparison and validates every field on the way back from a row, so a tampered row fails to reconstruct. - @register lives only in the package __init__, never a submodule. - Lint only the changed files (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors on main); do not run --stdin-filename.
project_specification.constraints: - Feature 326 adds exactly one new module (risk.demotion), one new table (risk_signal_demotion), one new value (SignalDemotion), one new store (RiskSignalDemotionStore) and one new error class (RiskSignalDemotionError, a sibling of RiskStoreError) — and nothing else. It does not add a new kill, a new flatten, a new halt, a new component, a new table column on another member's table, or a new seat accessor. - The demotion reaches the retention ratio through the forward member's public module-level function forward_ic_retention, never importing the forward member's tables, never naming its columns (live_ic, backtest_ic) and never reading forward_record itself. The store's record method takes the node_id and the ratio as arguments; the caller obtains the ratio from the forward member. The forward member's behaviour, messages, codes and tests are untouched. - The demotion is persisted in a table of this feature's own, not a column on forward_record and not a row in risk_order_kill. The table holds one row per signal (primary key node_id), monotone per signal. - The comparison is strictly `<` against DEMOTION_BOUND (0.4); a ratio exactly at 0.4 is held, not demoted. - The demotion moment is read back from the standing row, never stamped. - First-write-wins per signal: a second demotion writes nothing and returns the standing demotion with changed=False. - The forward member's behaviour, messages, codes and tests are untouched; feature 337's existing behaviour is relied upon and not duplicated. - No order-sensitive shared file is edited (src/app/middleware.py, src/app/settings.py, migrations/versions/**, alembic/versions/** are excluded from this feature's file claim). The schema is created idempotently on connect, so no migration is edited.
project_specification.test_baseline: - All existing tests in the risk member (packages/risk/tests) and in tests/ continue to pass. Feature 326's new suite is packages/risk/tests/test_demotion.py, added beside them. - The forward member's suite (packages/forward/tests) continues to pass unchanged; feature 326 reads through forward_ic_retention and does not add or alter any forward test. - Run the member's suite (uv run pytest packages/risk/tests) and the repository-level suite, and confirm all pass.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1 — the module. Create packages/risk/src/risk/demotion.py with: the DEMOTION_BOUND constant (0.4); RISK_SIGNAL_DEMOTION_TABLE = "risk_signal_demotion"; the DDL (node_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, retention_ratio REAL NOT NULL, demotion_bound REAL NOT NULL CHECK (demotion_bound > 0), supervisor_process_id TEXT NOT NULL, demoted_at TEXT NOT NULL, plus CHECK that retention_ratio is a finite real); a frozen value SignalDemotion (node_id, ratio, bound, demoted_at, supervisor_process_id, sequence, changed) whose __post_init__ validates the node as a signal identity, the ratio as a finite real, the bound as strictly positive, the instant as aware, and re-derives the ratio < bound comparison, refusing a demotion whose ratio is not below its bound; a store RiskSignalDemotionStore with record (judging the ratio against DEMOTION_BOUND, persisting when below, reading demoted_at back from the standing row, first-write-wins per signal) and demotions / demotion_for reads; and the module-level spellings record_signal_demotion and recorded_signal_demotions. The demotion moment is read back from the standing row via a SELECT of the row's own demoted_at after the insert, never stamped. Refusals: node not a signal identity and ratio not a number in RiskSignalDemotionError; address and persistence faults in RiskStoreError.

Phase 2 — the error class. Add RiskSignalDemotionError to packages/risk/src/risk/errors.py as a sibling of RiskStoreError, with the greppable token SIGNAL_DEMOTION_CODE = "signal_demotion", and document it in the module docstring's taxonomy. Export it from the member's __init__.

Phase 3 — the member surface. In packages/risk/src/risk/__init__.py, import the new module's public names, add them to __all__, and register the demotion store as a component under DEMOTION_COMPONENT_NAME = "risk-signal-demotion" with a build_signal_demotion_store builder that resolves DATABASE_URL and returns None when no store is named.

Phase 4 — the suite. Create packages/risk/tests/test_demotion.py asserting every claim in the test_baseline, organised around the sentence's claims, each refusal in its own test named by its grep token. Include the cross-member test: a real second interpreter computes the retention ratio through forward_ic_retention and this feature judges it and persists the demotion, asserting the demotion carries the ratio the forward member computed.

Phase 5 — validate and run. Validate the spec (claw-forge validate-spec), then run the member's suite (uv run pytest packages/risk/tests) and the repository-level suite, and lint only the changed files. Confirm all pass.
